newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 31.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 31. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong Moslem group Nahdlatul Ulama, appeared together at a mass prayer session in the Central Java capital of Semarang with army chief-of-staff Hartono and President Suharto's eldest daughter and stalwart of the ruling Golkar party Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana. Around 75,000 people are said to have attended the gathering.
Speedy trials were staged on Saturday for the 30 people arrested after rioting in the central Javan town of Pekalongan last week which targeted ethnic Chinese and left dozens of buildings damaged.
Economists says managers in the Indonesian civil service need to attack corruption after the country was named the most corrupt in Asia in an annual survey by a Hong Kong-based consultancy.
Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer PT Astra International made a net profit of around 470 billion rupiah in 1996.
